newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Quebrada Blanca '96 copper output climbs.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Quebrada Blanca '96 copper output climbs.

text.p: Canadian-owned copper mine Quebrada Blanca reported cathode production climbing last year to 67,737 tonnes from 46,352 tonnes in 1995, said pit general manager James Drake.
The mine, which came on stream two years ago, should reach design capacity of 75,000 tonnes a year in 1997, said Drake.
"We're almost there. In December we were a little over design capacity and in January a little under," he told Reuters.
Vancouver-based Cominco Ltd, Cominco Resources and Teck Resources International hold a 76.5 percent stake in the mine which lies on a plateau near the Bolivian border.

Built at a head-spinning 4,400 meters (14,400 feet) above sea-level, the mine suffered a slow start-up because of problems in adapting its newly developed heap-leaching technology to the harsh weather conditions at the pit.
